title: Crafting Blockchain Policy Framework for India

ms.promise:
1.Comprehensive list of stakeholders:
・A list of a minimum of 15 stakeholders, including government agencies, blockchain enterprises, and legal experts.
・Each stakeholder will be identified by name, role, and organization.

2.Initial research report:
・A comprehensive report detailing existing blockchain policies, gaps in Indian regulations, and the needs of stakeholders.

3.Organize at least 3 stakeholder workshops:
・Workshops will be virtual, each attended by at least 10 participants representing key sectors.
・Workshops will gather insights on the current regulatory framework and blockchain development.
ms.criteria:
1.Stakeholder list:
・Completion is defined as having a minimum of 15 verified stakeholders across different sectors.

2.Initial research report:
・A comprehensive report covering an overview of current regulations, identifying gaps, and summarizing stakeholder needs.

3.Workshops:
・At least 3 workshops, each lasting a minimum of 1 hour, with at least 10 participants.
・Workshops will focus on gathering insights on policy issues and blockchain development.
・Advertising materials and participation details (Registration form link) will be prepared.
ms.report:
A. Output: Comprehensive Stakeholder List
A comprehensive stakeholder list was prepared with a minimum of 15 stakeholders relevant to the development of a Blockchain Policy Framework for India.
The stakeholder list includes individuals and organizations across multiple relevant sectors, including government/policy ecosystem, blockchain enterprises, legal experts, technical experts, academic institutions, Web3 ecosystem participants and industry practitioners.
Each stakeholder has been identified with relevant details such as name, role/designation, organization and stakeholder category.
Acceptance criteria: 
Completion is defined as having a minimum of 15 verified stakeholders across different sectors.
The stakeholder list meets the acceptance criteria by including stakeholders across:
・Government / policy ecosystem
・Blockchain and Web3 enterprises
・Legal and policy experts
・Technical experts
・Academic and research institutions
・Crypto / digital asset ecosystem participants

Evidence: Stakeholder List Attached
B. Output: Initial Research Report
The Initial Research Report for the Blockchain Policy Framework for India was completed.
The report provides an overview of the current blockchain and digital asset policy landscape, identifies gaps in Indian regulations and summarizes key stakeholder needs relevant to blockchain development, crypto asset regulation, compliance, taxation, data protection, governance and innovation.
The report also considers comparative international approaches and identifies policy issues requiring further stakeholder consultation.
Acceptance criteria: 
Completion is defined as a comprehensive report covering:
・Overview of current blockchain and digital asset regulations
・Gaps in Indian regulatory treatment
・Stakeholder needs and ecosystem concerns
・Relevant policy issues around blockchain development
・Areas requiring further consultation and validation
